findings: VideoIndex::isValid returns true if open fails, explicitly treating inaccessible input as not an inspected error. It cannot be interpreted as successfully verified content. No unavailable-file runtime check performed.

verify_v2 checks header compatibility and trailing cbir marker for nonempty indexes, but does not parse frame deltas/hash payload. load_v2 parses frame/hash payload but does not read/check trailer. These are distinct evidence scopes; one does not prove the other.

V2 header checks endianness and scalar sizes, so opposite-endian storage is refused rather than translated. It stores delta-varints plus native64-bit hashes; no source-content fingerprint/version identity embedded beyond program version metadata.

load_v2 caps declared numFrames to MAX_FRAMES_PER_VIDEO but sizes packed buffer from packedLen and has no explicit shift-depth bound in varint loop. Structural bounds/corrupt-input behavior not executed; no malformed-memory or ASAN probing.

save_v1 limits count using INT16_MAX while warning says65k; frame values use uint16 and separately check UINT16_MAX. Old-format count and frame-number limits differ. V1 load repair inserts a zero-hash frame0 for nonzero first-frame history; these repaired values are not decoded frame observations.
save opens destination directly for writing and removes it on save_v2 failure, unlike separate temporary replacement utility. No failure/crash test or real cache overwrite performed.

Migration verifies converted count/data before replacement and attempts backup restoration on rename failure. Dry run uses fixed temp pathname and may inspect/write conversion artifacts; no migration command executed. Error removal counter has duplicate increment in load_v1 failure branch, so summary may differ from successful removals.

Unit tests cover legacy fixtures, empty/truncated files and synthetic small/large offset roundtrips. They require TEST_DATA_DIR and mutate temporary-named files within that corpus; read only here. They do not establish decoder temporal recall, every malformed format, opposite endianness, or crash durability.
